title: Museum of Haunted History To Open in St. Petersburg, Showcasing Paranormal Artifacts and Experiences
excerpt: Dr. Brandy Stark, founder of Spirits of St. Petersburg, will soft open the Museum of Haunted History at 4754 1st Ave. N. on Friday and Saturday, Oct. 23 and 24,...
content:
Dr. Brandy Stark, founder of Spirits of St. Petersburg, will soft open the Museum of Haunted History at 4754 1st Ave. N. on Friday and Saturday, Oct. 23 and 24, from 6 to 9 p.m. The museum sits inside a 1939 bungalow in the Central Oak Park neighborhood.

Visitors will see haunted and historic objects. One is a wedding dress tied to a spirit named Irene. Others include antiques, dolls, and artifacts from past investigations. The house will also hold a spiritual apothecary and space for psychic readings, workshops, meetings, and future overnight investigations.

Stark's books, crystals, pendulums, Stay Spooky St. Pete merchandise, and a few dolls will be for sale. More is on the way: a Little Free Library of Supernatural Stuff, a supernatural trinket trade drawer, and a windphone. That last item is an old-fashioned telephone made for quiet thought, or for anyone who wants to talk to a loved one who has died.

"I've always wanted to present the supernatural in a manner that, number one, is safe, number two, is educational, and number three, is a little bit of fun," Stark said in a conversation with St. Pete Rising.

Stark has studied paranormal activity since 1997. She has led local ghost tours and looked into hundreds of cases. She also wrote Supernatural St. Petersburg and Paranormal Pinellas Vol. 1 & 2.

She also hopes to use salvaged doors, windows, lampshades, doorknobs, and other building pieces. Some will come from places the group has investigated. Others will come from buildings facing demolition.

"Part of my goal is to also turn this museum into an architectural statement," Stark said. "It's a way to keep the property and its legend alive, and to make the building itself an exhibit, in addition to the exhibits inside."

Group members think the bungalow may have a resident spirit of its own. During an early walkthrough, one team member sensed someone in the house. Since then, the group has recorded what they believe are unexplained voices and replies through a spirit box. They have casually named the presence William, perhaps after the home's first owner.

At first, the museum will open Fridays through Sundays. Exact hours are still being sorted out. It will also be home base for Spirits of St. Petersburg, where members can go over evidence, host classes, and keep ghost tours and investigations running.

A grand opening is planned for February 2027, along with Stark's annual Valentwe'en art show. The next show, titled Love Letters to the Dearly Departed, will ask artists and guests to honor celebrities and public figures who have died. Down the road, the detached garage will become an artist studio for rent.
